suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add convention note: when splitting a monolithic file into modules, internal items that need cross-module access within the crate should use `pub(crate)` visibility rather than `pub`. Only items that were previously in the public API should be re-exported via `pub use` from lib.rs.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: All three split features (split-launa-core, split-launa-esp-ota, split-launa-sim) followed this pattern correctly, but it could be codified as a convention for future splits.

rejectedObservations.observation: Update architecture.md to reflect new module structure in launa-sim and launa-esp-ota
rejectedObservations.reason: already-documented — architecture.md already describes the module structures and internal organization of these crates

rejectedObservations.observation: frame_gen/physics modules in launa-sim could use 'pub(crate) mod' instead of 'pub mod'
rejectedObservations.reason: ambiguous — using 'pub mod' with 'pub(crate)' items is a valid and common Rust pattern. The external visibility of the module name is harmless since items within are not externally accessible. Not worth codifying a preference.
